title: perf(canary): automated detection for latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Priya Rao
description:
Motivation: We need tighter, automated detection of performance regressions during canary rollouts to avoid customer-facing latency spikes and throughput regressions. This PR implements a runtime-integrated detector that evaluates latency and throughput metrics against adaptive thresholds, introduces hysteresis to avoid flapping, and wires rollout guard logic into the canary controller so rollouts automatically pause and rollback on confirmed regressions.

What this changes: - Adds a new perf-canary detector service (redwood/perf/canary/detector) that ingests upstream trace/metric summaries and computes regression scores using configurable baselines and EWMA-based smoothing. - Implements adaptive thresholding tied to baseline percentiles and estimated variance so detection sensitivity adjusts per workload. - Introduces hysteresis windows and minimum sample counts before triggering a pause/rollback to prevent noisy signals from aborting healthy rollouts. - Extends the existing canary controller (redwood/serving/canary_controller.go) with rollout guards and automated rollback paths for critical regressions. - Adds config knobs to console and API for canary sensitivity, minimum sample sizes, latency/throughput thresholds, and KV-cache-aware detection modes. - Adds e2e perf-canary tests (perf-canary/integration) that simulate degraded nodes and validate automated pause/rollback behavior.

Design notes: - Detection is based on two signals: p95 latency and effective throughput (tokens/sec per GPU). Both are compared to a dynamic baseline computed from recent steady-state traffic. A regression score is computed as a weighted combination; a score above the configured guard threshold triggers the guard. - Hysteresis: two-stage confirmation (detect -> confirm) where confirm requires sustained deviation for N intervals. This reduces flapping while preserving responsiveness. - KV-cache-aware mode: for workloads where prefix cache hit-rate heavily affects latency, the detector incorporates prefix hit-rate into the regression score so cache churn doesn't cause false positives. - Rollout actions: on confirmed regression the controller will (1) pause traffic shift, (2) optionally rollback to previous model variant, (3) emit detailed audit event and slack alert, (4) annotate canary and create an incident Linear ticket if configured.

Compatibility and safety: - Feature gated behind "perf_canary_auto_detect" feature flag. Default sensitivity set to conservative values to avoid false positives. - We fall back to human review if minimum sample counts aren't met. - No changes to public API surface other than new canary config fields.

Testing and rollout: - Unit tests for detector logic and scoring (coverage added). - Integration tests simulate noisy KV cache, cold caches, and node degradation. - Manual staging run on dedicated cluster to validate thresholds against real traffic.

Related: ENG-4921 (automated perf detection), ENG-4987 (canary rollback automation). Links: docs/perf/canary.md for operator docs and console PR updates in redwood-console (coming).

release_notes: Adds automated performance canary detection and rollout guards (feature-flagged). Operators can configure sensitivity, hysteresis windows, and KV-cache-aware detection. Default conservative settings; no breaking changes.
notes_for_operators: Feature flag: perf_canary_auto_detect (off by default for existing clusters)
Default sensitivity is conservative; tune via canary.sensitivity.{latency,throughput} in canary config
KV-cache-aware mode enabled with canary.cache_awareness: true
Minimum sample counts default to 200 requests per interval to avoid noisy detections
Rollouts will pause by default; automatic rollback is opt-in via canary.automated_rollback=true
